DEN_Refugee
Alfira is a tiefling bard in Baldur's Gate 3. She is at the Emerald Grove on a cliff overlooking the ritual, trying to compose a song.
“
Dance upon the stars tonight... Smile and pain will fade away... Words of mine will turn to ash... When you call the last light down...
„
— Alfira, composing a ballad

Overview

Background

Alfira is part of the group of tiefling refugees who were exiled from Elturel, and Bardic apprentice to a woman named Lihala. On the journey to the Emerald Grove, they were attacked by gnolls and Lihala was killed. Alfira has since been trying to compose a eulogy for her.

Involvement

Act One

The party can find Alfira on the hill overlooking the druidic shrine circle at the Emerald Grove. She is frustrated over a lack of progress in composing a song for her recently deceased teacher, Lihala. The party may choose to help by inspiring her.

Performing together

If a party member offers aid by performing with Alfira, they receive Lihala's lute and can attempt to play along with her:

  • Alfira
    Dance upon the stars tonight... Smile and pain will fade away...
    • [PERFORMANCE] Play along with her.  (DC 15)
      • Alfira
        Words of mine will turn to ash... When you call the last light down...
        • [PERFORMANCE] Keep time with her. (DC 10)

Succeeding both checks (one failure allows a retry) helps Alfira make significant progress in composing her song. The party member who helped her gains  Musical Instruments proficiency, if they did not have it already. Bards are not required to make ability checks to assist her.

Encouraging with words

If a party member offers aid by encouraging Alfira with words, she becomes inspired and a cutscene plays where she performs her near-finished song for the party. This does not reward the musical instrument proficiency.

The Weeping Dawn

After helping her in either way, she titles her song The Weeping Dawn and confesses in tears she was with her teacher Lihala when they were ambushed by gnolls, and has been struggling to create a worthy eulogy for her. The party can also gain the ⁠A Bard's Muse inspiration ( Entertainer background). Alfira remains in this location, giving her song the finishing touches and singing it periodically.

Not helping Alfira

If the player character or their companions choose not to help, they may leave, convince her to give up, insult her, or steal / destroy her lute with the following options:

  • Slip the lute into your pack.
  • [DEXTERITY] Snatch the lute out of her hands and smash it. (DC 10)
  • You want honesty? Give up - you don't have the makings of a bard.
  • You're holding yourself back. Start over with a blank slate.
  • Here. I don't have time for this.

Celebration in the camp

If Alfira is still alive after the party return from the Goblin Camp, she moves to the other tieflings who are getting ready to leave for the Campsite. At the celebration, she talks to  Lakrissa and, if spoken with, offers to compose a song about the player character and their deeds.

After the party, Alfira leaves with the other tieflings and can be met later in Act Two.

During ⁠Raid the Emerald Grove, Alfira's corpse is with those of the tiefling children in the Tiefling Hideout.

The Dark Urge

If the  Dark Urge is chosen as Origin, Alfira visits the camp shortly after crossing the bridge to the Blighted Village, whether she has been spoken with or not. Regardless of the player character's choice to allow her to spend the night at camp or not, they wake up to find her disemboweled by their own hands, earning the ⁠Snipping the Chords inspiration. They can decide whether or not to hide the evidence, embrace their handiwork (which causes Paladins to break their Oath) or be horrified by it.

To keep Alfira alive, she must be  knocked out in the Emerald Grove before taking the long rest that triggers her visit. If Alfira is already dead, knocked out, or otherwise unavailable immediately prior to the party's committing to a long rest, she is replaced by the dragonborn bard  Quil.

This event may be delayed by others. For example, if Karlach is recruited before Wyll, his arrival takes precedence as the camp event that night and Quil arrives the following night instead. To ensure her survival (especially in honour mode) it may be necessary to knock out Alfira more than once. The trigger is crossing the bridge over the river towards the Blighted Village, after the game auto-saves.[verify] Going to Wakeen's Rest does not trigger the scene on long rest.

When the long rest is completed and Alfira has survived the night, she returns to where she was knocked out and can later be met at the camp celebration. After that she can be seen again in Act Two.

Act Two

In Act Two, Alfira is inside the Last Light Inn sitting by the fire at X: -66 Y: 142. If spoken to, she recounts being ambushed by cultists of the Absolute and that some of the tieflings were taken to Moonrise Towers. This starts the ⁠Rescue the Tieflings quest. Giving a hopeful response awards the ⁠A Smile Better Suits... inspiration ( Folk Hero background). If Lakrissa is saved along with the other tieflings, Alfira rewards the  Potent Robe and other loot to the party.

If she survives to the end of Act Two, Alfira moves to Moonrise Towers. A conversation reveals that she wants to use her music to help calm the tiefling children in the room with her. If the active character is a Bard, they can speak with her again to gain the  Improved Bardic Inspiration (class action) class action; it is not necessary to perform the song.

Act Three

If she survives to Act Three, Alfira journeys to the rooftop of Elfsong Tavern. Reuniting with her awards the following inspiration:

  • ⁠Finding her Stage ( Entertainer background)
  • ⁠Safeguarding the Songbird ( Folk Hero background)

If Lakrissa survives as well, she waits tables at the Elfsong, and may occasionally be found on the roof with Alfira. The two of them reveal they are dating, and that Alfira is planning on opening a bardic school.

Speak with Dead

Alfira's corpse can be communed with using  Speak with Dead.

Below are the available dialogue if Alfira is killed in camp by the  Dark Urge.

  • Who are you?
    • Alfira
      Alfira... apprentice... bard...
  • Did you have any valuables?
    • Alfira
      Lihala's lute... where is... where...
  • Where were you going?
    • Alfira
      Elfsong Tavern... Baldur's Gate...
      • Why the Elfsong Tavern?
        • Alfira
          To perform there... to sing... for Lihala...
  • Did you come here alone?
    • Alfira
      With... Lihala... but... but...
      • Who is Lihala?
        • Alfira
          Teacher... friend... everything to me. But gnolls... ripped her... apart...
          • You met gnolls? How did you survive?
            • Alfira
              Run when they... shriek. They call... for others...

Idle banter

Act Three

Alfira can be met on the roof of the Elfsong Tavern in Act Three where she has idle conversations with Lakrissa.

  • Alfira
    How's your shift going?
  • Lakrissa
    A rich arsehole sent his drink back three times - so I spat in his last one.
  • Alfira
    Lakrissa!
  • Lakrissa
    He said it was 'delicious'.
  • Alfira
    Rent is due soon. I was thinking I could do some busking?
  • Lakrissa
    No need, I picked up some extra shifts.
  • Alfira
    You didn't have to do that.
  • Lakrissa
    I know - I wanted to. You just focus on your music.
  • Alfira
    We made it, Lakrissa.
  • Lakrissa
    Damn right - and not even pissy druids or cursed shadows could stop us.
  • Alfira
    Only because I had you.
  • Lakrissa
    Nah - you'd have been fine without me. But the company was welcome.

Notes

  • Alfira may have originally been intended as a potential companion. In the game files, she is defined in Origins.lsx, which lists the origin characters as well as non-origin companions, hirelings, and a few related characters such as  Losiir. In the file, she is listed with the Entertainer background and the College of Lore subclass.
    • Since the release of patch 7, Alfira can be recruited as a temporary companion. However, per Larian's notes for this patch, she is only recruitable if the Dark Urge is chosen as origin and there is room for her in the active party. Alfira has the level progression of a generic NPC_Wizard and has less-than-complete functionality as a playable character. Known limitations include:
      • Not having the Dip, Help, or Hide actions (cannot use Stealth or Pickpocket)
      • Reduced hit point increases
      • Lacking Bard spells
      • Having a much higher Intelligence than Charisma
    • Mods or console commands are required to allow Alfira to become a permanent companion or grant her standard companion functionality – such as normal actions, hit point increases, and skills. Otherwise, she remains unable to function properly.
    • When Alfira joins the party, she has the Tiefling race applied to her a second time, granting her an 18 m (60 ft) movement speed.
  • Despite having the colouration of a Mephistopheles tiefling, Alfira (along with every other Tiefling refugee) is labelled an Asmodeus tiefling.
  • As part of the quality of life improvements in patch 6, which added the possibility of choosing which companion to dismiss while accepting a new one into the party, Alfira's game files seem to have gained some empty and unused dialogue lines related to being dismissed from the party.
  • Alfira's CharacterVisualResource is named S_DEN_Bard_4a405fba-3000-4c63-97e5-a8001ebb883c  with a UUID of 1ab11041-a5b8-7f62-ced5-a6bc1179c0e3
